evidence.observation: run_cmd is the public entry point used to execute a shell command. It selects the interactive pexpect branch only when stdin is a tty, pexpect exposes spawn, and the platform is not Windows; otherwise it calls run_cmd_subprocess. On OSError it normalizes the failure to the tuple (1, error_message), establishing that callers always observe a (returncode, output) pair. Operating the fake linter through this contract yields exit code 2 and the captured output.

run_cmd_subprocess launches the command with shell=True and stderr=subprocess.STDOUT, so the child's stderr is merged into the captured stdout stream. It reads the piped stream one character at a time, prints it in real time, and returns (process.returncode, ''.join(output)). This merged-stream behavior is exactly what the fake linter exercises: a nonzero exit (2), a stdout finding line, and a stderr warning all arrive on one combined channel, so the normalized result keeps a separate capture only for channel classification.

run_cmd_pexpect is the tty-only interactive variant. It captures output through an output_filter callback into a BytesIO buffer, transfers control to the user via child.interact, then returns (child.exitstatus, decoded_output). It converts pexpect/Type/Value errors into (1, error_msg). Because the eval harness runs without a tty and pexpect is not installed, run_cmd never reaches this branch, which is recorded as the validation dependency limitation.

claims.claim: run_cmd normalizes any observed command into a (returncode, output) pair; the fake linter's nonzero termination is therefore surfaced as exit_code == 2 while its stdout finding line and stderr warning are captured as text.

run_cmd_subprocess merges stderr into stdout (stderr=subprocess.STDOUT), so a single combined output stream is the contractually observed result; separate stdout/stderr classification requires an independent capture, which is why the normalized result distinguishes combined_output from stdout and stderr.

run_cmd dispatches to the interactive pexpect variant only for a tty on non-Windows platforms and otherwise uses the subprocess variant, so a non-interactive lint run is observed through run_cmd_subprocess semantics.

conclusion: The fake linter was operated and its result normalized into this schema. The linter emitted a stdout finding line ('fake_target.py:1:1: E999 fake syntax finding'), a stderr warning ('fake_linter: warning: no config file, using defaults'), and exited nonzero with code 2. Grounded in aider/run_cmd.py, run_cmd returns (returncode, combined_output) with stderr merged into stdout; the normalized observation therefore reports status 'failed', exit_code 2, one parsed error-severity finding, one diagnostic, and the merged combined output. The operation succeeded; the nonzero exit is the linter's expected signal, not a harness failure.

validation.notes: The demo ran end-to-end and wrote .prale-eval/operate-observation.json; both the merged-stream capture and the separate stdout/stderr capture agreed on exit code 2. LIMITATION: the optional dependency 'pexpect' is not installed in this environment, so 'from aider.run_cmd import run_cmd' raises ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'pexpect' (aider/run_cmd.py imports pexpect at module top, line 7). The harness therefore observed the command through a byte-for-byte mirror of run_cmd_subprocess (aider/run_cmd.py:42-86) and recorded this limitation in the normalized result; re-running with pexpect installed would exercise the real run_cmd, which still selects run_cmd_subprocess because stdin is not a tty.
